rows: Bay County: Lack of Documented Review of Required Quarterly Reports (federal, AL 97.036 FEMA Public Assistance)

3 of 40 quarterly FEMA (Hurricane Michael) reports prepared by the county's consultant did not match approved expenses and support. There was no documented county review before the consultant submitted them. Material weakness; no questioned costs.
/governments/bay-county#f-bay-county-fy2024-2024-001
Bay County: Ineligible Expenses Approved for Reimbursement (federal, AL 97.083 SAFER fire staffing grant)

Two of three reimbursement requests tested included ineligible payroll costs approved by the grant administrator. The federal grantor caught them and paid only eligible costs. Material weakness; no questioned costs.
/governments/bay-county#f-bay-county-fy2024-2024-002
Bay County: Material audit adjustments (Bay County financial statements)
Material adjustments were needed for the financial statements to meet GAAP because county controls did not catch them in time. Material weakness.
/governments/bay-county#f-bay-county-fy2024-2024-003
Bay County: Material adjustments - Bay County Property Appraiser
The Property Appraiser's office needed material adjustments to cash and accounts payable, and a check was improperly dated in its records. Material weakness.
/governments/bay-county#f-bay-county-fy2024-property-appraiser-2024-001
Bay County: Permit fees not charged per adopted fee schedule (first reported 2020)

Because of problems in the permit system, the county charged some permit fees that did not match the fee schedule set by Resolutions 3945 and 3957, overcharging in some cases; the county booked a payable for the estimated excess. Auditor recommended fixing the system and remedying affected permits.
/governments/bay-county#f-bay-county-fy2023-bay-county-2023-001
Bay County: Material adjustments - Bay County Sheriff
The Sheriff's office needed material adjustments to cash, expenses, unearned revenue, payables and accrued liabilities. Material weakness.
/governments/bay-county#f-bay-county-fy2023-sheriff-2023-001
Bay County: Permit fees not charged per adopted fee schedule (Resolution 3847)
Permit system errors caused some permits to be charged above the adopted fee schedule.
/governments/bay-county#f-bay-county-fy2022-bay-county-2022-001
Bay County: Inadequate review of component unit financial information
The county did not adequately review figures from a discretely presented component unit, so adjustments were needed. Significant deficiency.
/governments/bay-county#f-bay-county-fy2022-bay-county-2022-002
Bay County: Material adjustments - Bay County Sheriff (repeat of 2021-001)
Sheriff's office needed material audit adjustments.

Bay District Schools: Audit Adjusting Entries (first reported 2024)

Significant corrections were needed, including unearned state funds not identified, an unrecorded IT subscription agreement, misclassified capital spending, and OPEB, accrual and lease adjustments. The auditor ties it partly to a lack of appropriate staffing.
/governments/bay-district-schools#f-bay-district-schools-fy2025-2025-001
Bay District Schools: Expenditures not limited to budgeted amounts (first reported by Auditor General as AM 2023-001)

General Fund spending exceeded the budget in three functional categories by a total of $326,700, and the Board did not amend the budget by September 10 as state law and Board policy require. Caused by year-end adjustments not reflected in budget monitoring.
/governments/bay-district-schools#f-bay-district-schools-fy2025-2025-002
Bay District Schools: Return of Title IV funds worksheets not documented as independently reviewed (federal, Pell Grant, Haney Technical College)
Refunds of federal student aid were calculated correctly, but there was no sign-off showing an independent review. Material weakness; no questioned costs.
/governments/bay-district-schools#f-bay-district-schools-fy2025-2025-101
Bay District Schools: Return of Title IV funds not made within required timeline (federal, Pell Grant)

For 2 of 9 students tested, federal aid was returned to the U.S. Department of Education after the 45-day deadline because of manual-control human error. Could risk future Pell funding. Significant deficiency.
/governments/bay-district-schools#f-bay-district-schools-fy2025-2025-102
Bay District Schools: Multi-factor authentication not required for student information (federal, Pell / Gramm-Leach-Bliley)
The district's system did not require multi-factor authentication to access student information, as federal student-information security rules require. Material weakness.
/governments/bay-district-schools#f-bay-district-schools-fy2025-2025-103
Bay District Schools: Lack of Appropriate Staffing Leading to Audit Entries
Staffing shortfalls meant the district's own processes missed entries the auditors had to make. Material weakness.
/governments/bay-district-schools#f-bay-district-schools-fy2024-2024-001
Bay District Schools: Wage rate (Davis-Bacon) compliance (federal, COVID-19 Education Stabilization Fund AL 84.425)

Two construction contracts shifted mid-stream to federal pandemic funds lacked the required Davis-Bacon wage clause, and certified payrolls were not collected. Questioned costs: $773,629. Significant deficiency.
/governments/bay-district-schools#f-bay-district-schools-fy2024-2024-002
Bay District Schools: Expenditures not limited to budgeted amounts (repeat of AM 2023-001)
General Fund spending again exceeded budgeted function amounts without a timely Board amendment.
/governments/bay-district-schools#f-bay-district-schools-fy2024-2024-003
Bay District Schools: Budgetary controls
General Fund spending exceeded budgeted amounts in six functional categories by $9,532 to $218,198 (total $582,437) and the Board did not amend the budget by September 10.

State law (s. 163.387 F.S.) requires each taxing authority to pay its tax increment to the CRA by January 1. The county paid 4 days late and the city did not pay its own share before year end, leaving the CRA trust fund short about $122,929.
